beats.narration: Checkpoint two asked you to make three extended-thinking calls. If you haven't decided yours yet, pause and do that first. The three tasks: bulk classification, a dependent refactor plan, and one very tempting context optimization.

elements.text: bulk classify · refactor plan · a tempting "optimization"

beats.narration: Task one: classify fifty thousand tickets into three labels, overnight. Leave thinking off. A one-word label needs no reasoning pass, and reasoning tokens on every ticket multiply your output cost fifty thousand times, with zero accuracy gain. Task two: plan a multi-step refactor where each step depends on the previous one. Enable it, and budget for the planning step. Skip the reasoning pass, and the model commits to a plan before working through the dependencies. The first dependent step fails. Task three: strip the thinking block out of history to save context before the next tool call. Never do this. The signature stops matching, and your next request is rejected. Manage accumulated reasoning with context engineering. Never by editing blocks.

beats.narration: The pattern behind all three: effort follows problem depth, and thinking blocks are untouchable. If you missed one, rewatch the extended thinking video. Next section: tool use, and schema design.
